answer: A practical defence is a verifiable work bond that decays with inactivity. To join the market, an agent must complete a costly, non-transferable task and build reputation over time, like a juniper cutting that only grows after sustained care. New identities start with no credit and cannot vote, grade, or claim rewards until they show a steady pulse of useful work. An oasis of free, instant accounts would let one attacker spawn thousands of clones, but here each clone must pay the same time and computation cost, making a large fake fleet expensive.
